methodology.equation: Primary and joint models: hourly whole-machine price = A × ∏(feature/reference)^exponent. Ordinary least squares on natural logarithms; predictions estimate the geometric price center. The separately labeled existing-method comparison retains a CPU baseline plus a multiplicative GPU increment, refitting both stages for each holdout.
methodology.cpuValidation: Five deterministic folds of whole provider × machine families; no family appears in its training and test data.
methodology.gpuValidation: Leave one entire provider × machine family out, holding every size and GPU configuration in that family together.
methodology.displayedCpu: The website displays the fixed RAM + CPU Geekbench model to retain a measured performance variable. Five whole-family folds validate that fixed formula; no nested feature selection is claimed. The broader RAM/vCPU capacity model and its nested selection results remain saved separately in cpu.selected for comparison.
methodology.primarySelection: CPU candidates share the full source-normalized RAM/vCPU cohort; GPU candidates share the full whole-GPU FP32/vCPU/GPU-count cohort. Sparse Geekbench and memory variants are evaluated separately. Missingness is never allowed to give one competing primary candidate an easier test set.
methodology.uncertainty: Reported errors use nested family holdouts for primary selection, not independent prospective data. Provider/GPU-model holdouts are additional fixed-feature diagnostics. No parameter confidence intervals are estimated for these feature-selection experiments.
methodology.memory: RAM and VRAM use source-normalized nominal GiB under the existing documented conventions: Google pricing GB are JEDEC binary; Azure explicitly decimal GB are converted using 10^9/2^30. These provider conventions do not establish identical usable device memory. Unspecified GB stay missing only for models requiring that variable, and do not block vCPU/FP32-only models. Google convention: https://cloud.google.com/products/compute/gpus-pricing; Azure convention: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/sizes/gpu-accelerated/nca100v4-series.
methodology.fp32: Dense conventional FP32 theoretical peak TFLOPS, excluding tensor TF32, reduced precision and sparse modes. Whole identical GPU allocations sum device peaks; this is aggregate arithmetic capacity, not a claim of measured application or multi-GPU scaling.
methodology.cpu: vCPU count is advertised capacity, not a cross-architecture performance benchmark. CPU Geekbench remains measured exact-shape Geekbench 6 Linux without SME; GPU Geekbench is a single-device Geekbench 7 OpenCL model proxy.
methodology.scope: Positive public hourly whole-machine prices observed within 36 hours. Shared/burstable CPU plans, unsupported accelerators and fractional/unknown GPU allocations are excluded. Storage/network bundles, power limits, provider margins and historical benchmark-region differences remain uncontrolled.
methodology.interpretation: Good fit means held-out MAPE ≤15% and log R² ≥0.8; approximate means ≤35% and ≥0.5, with at least 80% test coverage, 10 tested rows and four held-out groups. These descriptive thresholds are not guarantees. Exponents are associations, not marginal provider charges.

comparisons.note: Exploratory fixed-method comparison on the same configurations: retain the previous CPU-baseline + GPU-increment structure, then add FP32 to or replace GPU Geekbench in its multiplicative increment. Every outer fold excludes its entire family from both stages, including the CPU-only baseline data. Nonpositive residual prices reject the whole fold; no difficult rows are silently dropped. This follow-up does not change the prespecified broad-model selection pool or its nested headline error. Its errors condition on this fixed method; they are not the previous nested method-selection error.
